name: @heyrmes/mcp

tools.name: create_business
tools.description: Create a new business under the authenticated user's agency. Requires an active Agency plan subscription or admin role. Returns the new business ID for use in all subsequent tools. Only name is required.

tools.name: delete_business
tools.description: Permanently delete a business and all associated data, including agents, contacts, conversations, integrations, and related records. Requires admin access on the business. This is destructive and irreversible.

tools.name: list_businesses
tools.description: List all businesses the authenticated user can access. Admins see all businesses; regular users see only businesses linked via BusinessUser. Optional search filters by name, email, industry, or ID. Call this first to obtain business_id values.

search.description: Optional search text for name, email, industry, or ID.

limit.description: Maximum businesses to return. Defaults to 50.

tools.name: create_agent
tools.description: Create a new agent workflow inside a business. The agent starts with an empty or default flow, and the backend/UI adds a default TriggerAgent node on first load. Returns agent_id for channel and node operations. Agent is active by default unless active: false is passed.

active.description: Initial active state. Defaults to true.

tools.name: delete_agent
tools.description: Permanently delete an agent and its workflow from a business. Does not delete the business or any other agents.

tools.name: list_agents
tools.description: List all agents in a business, scoped by business_id rather than agency. Returns agent IDs, names, and active status. Use include_all_folders: true, the default, to include agents in subfolders. Call after list_businesses to get agent_id values.

include_all_folders.description: Include agents in subfolders. Defaults to true.

tools.name: set_agent_active_status
tools.description: Explicitly turn an agent ON or OFF. Sets active to the exact boolean provided; this is not a toggle. Use active: true to enable the agent for inbound triggers and execution, or active: false to disable it. Requires business and agent IDs.

tools.name: create_agent_channel
tools.description:
Create a new top-level channel wrapper on an agent's workflow. This is NOT the same as adding a node inside an existing channel subgraph — use create_channel_node for that. 

PROVIDER SELECTION (required reasoning step before calling this tool):
1. Always call list_channel_types first. Check requires_provider and provider_options in the response.
2. Map user-named providers to canonical values: 'LeadConnector'/'GoHighLevel'/'GHL' -> provider='ghl', 'HubSpot' -> provider='hubspot', 'Twilio' -> provider='twilio'.
3. Prefer provider-specific channel types (GHLWebChatChannel, HubSpotLiveChatChannel, TwilioSMSChannel, etc.) over generic ones when they exist. Pass the matching provider either way.
4. If the channel type has a provider param and no provider was specified by the user, call list_business_integrations to identify the connected provider. If ambiguous, ask the user before creating.
5. Do NOT create a channel without provider when requires_provider is true.

WEBCHAT/LIVE CHAT EXAMPLES:
- LeadConnector/GHL: channel_type='GHLWebChatChannel' provider='ghl' (fallback: 'WebChatChannel'/'LiveChatChannel' + provider='ghl').
- HubSpot: channel_type='HubSpotLiveChatChannel' provider='hubspot' (fallback: 'LiveChatChannel' + provider='hubspot').

AFTER CREATION: call get_agent_channel_settings to verify param_values.provider. If provider_missing is true, call update_agent_channel_settings immediately. Then build the subgraph, call validate_agent_channel, and save_agent_channel.

channel_type.description: Template ID from list_channel_types. Always call list_channel_types first.

channel_name.description: Canvas label for the channel instance.

provider.description: Canonical provider for provider-capable channel types. Use 'ghl' for LeadConnector/GoHighLevel, 'hubspot' for HubSpot, 'twilio' for Twilio. Required when the selected channel_type exposes a provider param (check requires_provider in list_channel_types) or when the user specified a provider.

tools.name: get_agent_channel
tools.description: Return the complete channel wrapper node and its full subgraph, including every node and edge inside the channel. Also hydrates the in-memory draft cache for subsequent edit operations. Call this before editing a channel if you have not edited it yet in the current MCP session, or to inspect current database state.

tools.name: list_agent_channels
tools.description: List all channel instances configured on a specific agent. Returns summary per channel: ID, type, label, provider, subgraph size, and whether required params such as provider, phone number, or HubSpot account are filled. Use channel_id from this response for all subgraph editing tools.

tools.name: list_channel_types
tools.description: List every channel type template available for agent workflows (not instances). Always call this BEFORE create_agent_channel to choose the correct channel_type and determine whether provider is required. The response includes requires_provider (true when a provider param exists on the schema), provider_options (allowed values when the schema exposes them), recommended_provider_values, and provider_selection_hint for each type. Channel creation is not complete until all required params including provider are set. Do not infer provider from display name alone — use provider_options and recommended_provider_values here.

tools.name: remove_agent_channel
tools.description: Permanently remove a channel instance from an agent's top-level workflow. Deletes the channel wrapper node and all edges connected to it. Does not delete the agent. Persists immediately to the database and clears any in-memory draft for that channel.

tools.name: get_workflow_node_schema
tools.description: Return the complete schema for a single workflow node type: all params with types, options, defaults, visibility rules, inputs, outputs, UI metadata, tool usage flags, and integration requirements. Call before create_channel_node or update_channel_node when configuring an unfamiliar node inside a channel subgraph. For nodes with dynamic outputs (Milestone, IfElse, splitters), pass representative params to get the resolved output handles.

node_type.description: Registry ID such as Conversation or Milestone.

params.description: Optional params used for dynamic schema resolution.

tools.name: list_workflow_node_types
tools.description: List all workflow node types that can be placed inside a channel subgraph (not channel wrappers, not TriggerAgent). Returns summaries with type ID, display name, category, inputs, outputs, param names, dynamic output support, and tool usage. Call before create_channel_node to find the correct node_type. These are subgraph node types — to find channel wrapper types, use list_channel_types instead.

tools.name: connect_channel_nodes
tools.description: Create a directed edge between two nodes inside a channel subgraph draft (channel_id from create_agent_channel or list_agent_channels). Operates inside the existing channel's data.subgraph — does not create channel wrappers. Source output connects to target input. If source_output or target_input are omitted, the tool auto-resolves handles using Heyrmes channel rules. For Milestone and IfElse branches, source_output must be the manual output name when auto-resolve cannot infer it. All draft changes must be saved with save_agent_channel.

source_output.description: Optional source handle or branch name.

tools.name: create_channel_node
tools.description: Add a new node inside an existing channel's subgraph (channel_id is from create_agent_channel or list_agent_channels). Does NOT create a new channel wrapper — use create_agent_channel for that. Changes are draft-only until save_agent_channel. Cannot create channel wrappers or TriggerAgent inside a subgraph. PhoneChannel subgraphs only allow ChannelStart and VoiceCall. For Milestone, IfElse, and ConversationalTrigger, pass manual_outputs to define branch names at creation time. Call get_workflow_node_schema before creating an unfamiliar node. All draft changes must be saved with save_agent_channel.

tools.name: disconnect_channel_nodes
tools.description: Remove all edges between two specified nodes in a channel subgraph draft (channel_id from create_agent_channel or list_agent_channels). Operates inside the existing channel's data.subgraph. Does not delete the nodes themselves. Draft-only until save_agent_channel.

tools.name: remove_channel_node
tools.description: Remove a node from a channel subgraph draft (channel_id from create_agent_channel or list_agent_channels), including all edges connected to it. Operates inside the existing channel's data.subgraph — does not remove the channel wrapper itself (use remove_agent_channel for that). Cannot remove ChannelStart. Draft-only until save_agent_channel.

tools.name: update_channel_node
tools.description: Update an existing node inside a channel's subgraph draft (channel_id from create_agent_channel or list_agent_channels). Operates on draft nodes — does not affect channel wrapper configuration. Can change label, merge param values, or replace manual outputs on branching nodes. Cannot modify ChannelStart. Changes are draft-only until save_agent_channel.

params.description: Param values to merge into data.paramValues.

tools.name: layout_channel_nodes
tools.description: Automatically arrange all nodes in a channel subgraph draft in a readable top-to-bottom DAG layout using topological layers (channel_id from create_agent_channel or list_agent_channels). Operates on the draft inside an existing channel's data.subgraph. Spacing defaults prevent overlap without excessive whitespace. Does not save — call save_agent_channel after layout.

tools.name: save_agent_channel
tools.description: Persist the channel subgraph draft to the database. Merges the draft subgraph into the channel wrapper node inside the agent's full flow, then PATCHes the agent workflow. By default, runs validation first and blocks save if there are errors. Always call validate_agent_channel and resolve all errors before saving. Do not use force: true to bypass a missing provider or other required configuration unless intentionally saving an incomplete draft. Clears the draft cache on successful save.

force.description: Save even when validation has errors. Defaults to false.

tools.name: validate_agent_channel
tools.description: Validate a channel's subgraph structure and channel wrapper configuration without saving. Returns errors and warnings with codes, messages, and affected node IDs. valid is true only when there are zero errors. Always call before save_agent_channel. Catches missing provider and other required wrapper params — when channel_not_configured is returned, details.missing_params lists the exact params to fix with update_agent_channel_settings.

tools.name: get_agent_channel_settings
tools.description: Return both layers of channel configuration: channel params stored on the channel wrapper (provider, phone number, HubSpot account ID, etc.) and objective settings from the Objective table (voice config, Hume, advanced behavior). Call immediately after create_agent_channel to verify param_values.provider is set before editing the subgraph. If provider_missing is true in the response, call update_agent_channel_settings to set param_values.provider before proceeding. Also call before update_agent_channel_settings to see current values and the valid params_schema.

tools.name: update_agent_channel_settings
tools.description:
Update channel configuration — the primary corrective tool when a channel was created without required params. Accepts partial updates to param_values on the channel wrapper (such as provider, from_number, hubspot_channel_account_id) and/or objective_settings for voice/Hume config and advanced behavior. Param changes persist immediately to the agent workflow. Objective settings persist immediately via the Objective API. Call get_agent_channel_settings first to see current values and valid param names. 
KEY PARAMS BY PROVIDER:
- GHL/LeadConnector: param_values.provider='ghl' (plus any channel-specific params shown in params_schema).
- HubSpot: param_values.provider='hubspot', param_values.hubspot_channel_account_id='<id>' when the schema requires it.
- Twilio: param_values.provider='twilio', param_values.from_number='<E.164-number>' when the schema requires it.

param_values.description: Values merged into channel data.paramValues. Use 'provider' key to set or fix the provider: 'ghl' for LeadConnector/GoHighLevel, 'hubspot' for HubSpot, 'twilio' for Twilio. Provider-specific params (from_number for Twilio, hubspot_channel_account_id for HubSpot) can be included in the same call.

objective_settings.description: Settings patch deep-merged by the Objective API.

tools.name: list_business_calendars
tools.description: List GoHighLevel calendars connected for a business. Used when configuring booking on Conversation, Milestone, or BookAppointment nodes. Requires GHL integration to be configured. Returns calendar IDs and names for use in node params or toolConfig.

tools.name: list_business_integrations
tools.description: List integration connection status for a business: which providers are configured, such as GoHighLevel/LeadConnector, HubSpot, Twilio, OpenAI, Claude, Google Calendar, Stripe, and others. Call this BEFORE creating provider-backed channels when the user did not explicitly name a provider. Use it to avoid assigning provider='hubspot' for a business that only has LeadConnector connected, or vice versa. Also call before booking/calendar nodes. Does not return raw secrets.

tools.name: list_cross_agent_handoff_targets
tools.description: List other agents in the same business, and their channel instances, that the current agent can hand off to via the Conversation node's Trigger Another Channel tool. Mirrors the UI behavior. Excludes the current agent. For each target agent, returns channel node IDs and types usable in handoff rules.
